transitions.historical_text: You can only activate this card while there is a face-up "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" on your side of the field. Destroy all monsters on your opponent's side of the field. No "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" can attack during the turn you activate this card.
transitions.summary: Era activation and restriction package, not a text erratum, spanning three concrete script differences: the GOAT script registers the 'no Blue-Eyes White Dragon can attack' lock at the end of s.activate (resolution) while the modern script registers it in s.cost, so under the era version a negated activation leaves no attack lock at all (upstream comment: 'If effect is negated, restriction doesn't apply'); the era lock omits EFFECT_FLAG_IGNORE_IMMUNE, so a Blue-Eyes immune to this card's effects can still attack ('If monsters are immuned, restruction doesn't apply'); and the era target function short-circuits to true where the modern one requires Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard(...,0,LOCATION_MZONE,1,nil), so the era card can be activated with the opponent controlling no monsters. No dated source for any of the three; chronology unresolved.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the current text (LCKC-EN025, Legendary Collection Kaiba Mega Pack)

transitions.historical_text: You can only activate this card while there is a face-up "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" on your side of the field. Destroy all monsters on your opponent's side of the field. No "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" can attack during the turn you activate this card.
transitions.modern_text: If you control "Blue-Eyes White Dragon": Destroy all monsters your opponent controls. "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" you control cannot attack the turn you activate this card.
transitions.summary: Wording modernisation across four printings (v2 DTP1-EN013 'Activate only while you control a face-up ...', v3 SDDC-EN025 PSCT colon form, v4 SDBE-EN021 plural 'Dragons' and no 'face-up', v5 LDK2-ENK19, v6 LCKC-EN025 'you control'). Recorded as cosmetic because no script encodes any of it: v6 narrows the attack lock on paper to Blue-Eyes you control, yet both the modern and the GOAT script register EFFECT_CANNOT_ATTACK_ANNOUNCE with SetTargetRange(LOCATION_MZONE,LOCATION_MZONE), i.e. both players' zones, and v4 drops 'face-up' from the activation condition while both scripts still require a face-up Blue-Eyes via aux.FaceupFilter.

review.notes: CONFLICT preserved rather than resolved: the printed lineage records two changes (v4 dropping 'face-up' in 2013, v6 adding 'you control' in 2018) that upstream's own modern script does not implement, so on the text alone v5->v6 would read as functional while on the script alone there is no difference at all to implement. I recorded it inside the cosmetic entry and flagged it; if the project later decides the printed text governs, v5->v6 should be promoted to functional with effective 2018-03-08 (introduces_version 6) and the baseline still serves every pre-2018 snapshot. Chain starts at v1 (DR2-EN150) because that is the text the goat cdb entry carries exactly, even though its printing (2005-10-20) is about six months after the 2005-04-01 GOAT snapshot; the printing in circulation then is v0 (AST-038, 2004-06-01), which differs only in 'No "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" can attack' vs '"Blue-Eyes White Dragon" cannot attack' - the same scope, so no era-mismatch flag. I read both scripts in full rather than relying on the diff; the only other differences are goat's missing EFFECT_FLAG_OATH (irrelevant once the lock is registered at resolution) and the RESET_PHASE+PHASE_END vs | spelling.
